violations.description: Three JSON columns store multi-value data in a single cell. attendees is a JSON array of user IDs, raci is a JSON object (R/A/C/I assignments), action_items is a JSON array of task objects. These cannot be queried, indexed, or joined without JSON path functions.
violations.sql_fix:
CREATE TABLE meeting_attendees (
  id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  meeting_id INT NOT NULL,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(),
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  UNIQUE KEY uq_meeting_attendee (meeting_id, user_id),
  CONSTRAINT fk_ma_meeting FOREIGN KEY (meeting_id) REFERENCES meetings(meeting_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT fk_ma_user FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE meeting_raci (
  id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  meeting_id INT NOT NULL,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  role ENUM('R','A','C','I') NOT NULL,
  created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(),
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  UNIQUE KEY uq_raci_meeting_user_role (meeting_id, user_id, role),
  CONSTRAINT fk_raci_meeting FOREIGN KEY (meeting_id) REFERENCES meetings(meeting_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT fk_raci_user FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE meeting_action_items (
  id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  meeting_id INT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  assigned_to INT NULL,
  due_date DATE NULL,
  status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
  created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(),
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  KEY idx_mai_meeting (meeting_id),
  CONSTRAINT fk_mai_meeting FOREIGN KEY (meeting_id) REFERENCES meetings(meeting_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT fk_mai_user FOREIGN KEY (assigned_to) REFERENCES users(user_id) ON DELETE SET NULL
);

ALTER TABLE meetings DROP COLUMN attendees, DROP COLUMN raci, DROP COLUMN action_items;

violations.description: line_total = quantity * unit_price. Fully derivable; stored on every INSERT and UPDATE. If either source column is corrected directly in DB without going through PHP, the stored total silently lies.
violations.php_change: Remove line_total from all INSERT/UPDATE payloads in AdminInvoiceController. Update SELECT queries that reference line_total directly — add (quantity * unit_price) AS line_total alias or use a generated column.

violations.description: All six financial summary columns on the invoice header are derived from invoice_items and the gst_rate. subtotal = SUM(item.quantity * item.unit_price), gst_amount = subtotal * gst_rate/100, cgst/sgst = gst_amount/2 (intra-state), igst = gst_amount (inter-state), total = subtotal + gst_amount + delivery_fee - discount. Stored on every create and update. Staleness risk is HIGH because the controller also stores rounded integer totals for e-invoicing which can diverge from item-level recalculation.
violations.sql_fix:
-- Recommended: keep these columns but make them GENERATED ALWAYS for consistency.
-- First, verify MySQL version supports generated columns, then:
ALTER TABLE invoices
  MODIFY COLUMN subtotal DECIMAL(12,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ii.quantity * ii.unit_price),0) FROM invoice_items ii WHERE ii.invoice_id = invoice_id)
  ) VIRTUAL,
  MODIFY COLUMN gst_amount DECIMAL(12,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ii.quantity * ii.unit_price),0) FROM invoice_items ii WHERE ii.invoice_id = invoice_id) * gst_rate / 100
  ) VIRTUAL;
-- NOTE: Correlated subqueries in generated columns require MySQL 8.0.19+. For MySQL 5.7, use a view instead:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_invoice_totals AS
  SELECT i.invoice_id,
         COALESCE(SUM(ii.quantity * ii.unit_price), 0) AS subtotal,
         COALESCE(SUM(ii.quantity * ii.unit_price), 0) * i.gst_rate / 100 AS gst_amount,
         COALESCE(SUM(ii.quantity * ii.unit_price), 0) * i.gst_rate / 200 AS cgst_amount,
         COALESCE(SUM(ii.quantity * ii.unit_price), 0) * i.gst_rate / 200 AS sgst_amount,
         0 AS igst_amount,
         COALESCE(SUM(ii.quantity * ii.unit_price), 0) * (1 + i.gst_rate/100) + COALESCE(i.delivery_fee,0) - COALESCE(i.discount,0) AS total
  FROM invoices i
  LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
  GROUP BY i.invoice_id;
violations.php_change: Pragmatic fix (lowest migration cost): keep columns but add a recalculate() helper that recomputes all six values from invoice_items before any GET response and asserts equality. On mismatch, log and auto-correct. This catches drift without rewriting the write path.

violations.description: subtotal = SUM(purchase_order_items.line_total), tax_amount = SUM(line_total * gst_rate/100 per item), total = subtotal + tax_amount + other_charges. All three stored on create and update.
violations.sql_fix:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_po_totals AS
  SELECT po.po_id,
         COALESCE(SUM(poi.quantity * poi.unit_price), 0) AS subtotal,
         COALESCE(SUM(poi.quantity * poi.unit_price * poi.gst_rate / 100), 0) AS tax_amount,
         COALESCE(SUM(poi.quantity * poi.unit_price), 0)
           + COALESCE(SUM(poi.quantity * poi.unit_price * poi.gst_rate / 100), 0)
           + COALESCE(po.other_charges, 0) AS total
  FROM purchase_orders po
  LEFT JOIN purchase_order_items poi ON poi.po_id = po.po_id
  GROUP BY po.po_id;

violations.description: All six are computed at payroll-run time: earned_salary = salary_per_day * present_days, overtime_salary = overtime_rate * overtime_hrs, total_salary = earned_salary + attend_bonus + overtime_salary + leave_salary + travel_allow, pf = earned_salary * (employees.pf_percent / 100), deductions = pf + professional_tax + deducted_advance, net_pay = total_salary - deductions. Stored by Payroll::upsert(). Payroll records are immutable after 'Paid' status so staleness risk is managed by workflow.
violations.sql_fix:
-- These are intentional snapshots of a payroll calculation. The correct fix is
-- NOT to drop them, but to ensure the payroll status machine prevents edits once
-- status = 'Processed' or 'Paid'. Add a DB-level check:
ALTER TABLE payroll ADD COLUMN is_locked TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 COMMENT 'Set to 1 when status reaches Paid; blocks further UPDATE';
-- Then in PHP, check is_locked before any UPDATE.
violations.php_change: Keep storing computed values (this is the payslip snapshot). Add AdminPayrollController::update() guard: reject edits when status='Paid'. Add is_locked column and CHECK constraint in application layer.

violations.description: These six columns mirror the corresponding salary fields from employees at payroll-run time. If an employee's salary is corrected for a past month, the payroll row stores the old rates. Columns lack the '_snapshot' or '_at_time_of_' suffix that would signal they are intentional snapshots.
violations.sql_fix:
-- No schema change needed — these ARE justified snapshots (pay-period salary snapshot).
-- Fix: rename columns to follow the snapshot naming convention:
ALTER TABLE payroll
  CHANGE COLUMN base_salary     base_salary_snapshot     DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00,
  CHANGE COLUMN site_allowance  site_allowance_snapshot  DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00,
  CHANGE COLUMN da              da_snapshot              DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00,
  CHANGE COLUMN food_allowance  food_allowance_snapshot  DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00,
  CHANGE COLUMN travel_allow    travel_allow_snapshot    DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00,
  CHANGE COLUMN overtime_rate   overtime_rate_snapshot   DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00;
violations.php_change: Update Payroll::upsert() to use the renamed column names. Update any SELECT queries in AdminPayrollController and reports that reference these columns.

violations.description: vendor_state mirrors vendors.state. If a vendor updates their state, existing POs show the new state rather than the state at PO creation time — which matters for GST (IGST vs CGST/SGST determination). Column name does not follow snapshot convention.
violations.sql_fix:
ALTER TABLE purchase_orders
  CHANGE COLUMN vendor_state vendor_state_snapshot VARCHAR(80) DEFAULT NULL
  COMMENT 'vendors.state at time of PO creation (GST determination)';
-- Backfill from vendors:
UPDATE purchase_orders po
  JOIN vendors v ON v.vendor_id = po.vendor_id
  SET po.vendor_state_snapshot = v.state
  WHERE po.vendor_state_snapshot IS NULL;
violations.php_change: Update AdminPurchaseOrderController::store() to reference vendor_state_snapshot. Update PurchaseOrder::create() INSERT. No logic change needed — just the column name.

violations.description: Six period-aggregate columns computed from invoices and payments data and stored via GstCompliance::saveSnapshot(). For status='draft'/'reviewed', these go stale immediately if an invoice is edited or a payment is voided after the snapshot. For status='filed'/'locked', staleness is intentional and legal. The risk window is the draft-to-filed gap.
violations.php_change: In AdminGstComplianceController::save(), record NOW() into snapshot_at. Show a warning in the API response when is_stale=1 and status is not 'filed'/'locked'. Expose an endpoint to re-snapshot before filing.

violations.description: All four are computed by AdminAttendanceController::calculateMetrics() from check_in, check_out, and the shift definition, then written on every INSERT/UPDATE. Recomputing from check_in/check_out/shift is fully deterministic. Storing them is a read-performance optimization that is reasonable given payroll depends on these values daily.

justified_exceptions.reason: Legally required GST invoice snapshot. Under CGST Act 2017, a tax invoice must show the buyer's name, address, and GSTIN as they were at the time of supply. Changing users.name or users.gst_number must not retroactively alter issued invoices.
Quotations and proformas also require customer details at issue time. A converted quotation that becomes an invoice must retain the original customer data used for pricing.
Price and GST rate at time of invoice. Products.base_price and gst_rate may change over time; the invoice must preserve what was charged.
Price and product configuration at time of order. product_configurations.price may change; the order must preserve what was agreed.

salary_per_day is the rate used for this payroll period (base_salary / working_days). It must be immutable once the payslip is issued. leave_credit and leave_availed are period-specific accrual state, not derived from a single source column.

Snapshot of stock levels that triggered the suggestion. Required for audit trail of why a suggestion was generated. RECOMMENDATION: rename to current_stock_snapshot and reorder_level_snapshot to follow project naming convention.

schema_defects.defect: Column name typo: total_salay should be total_salary, but total_salary already exists as a different column in the same table. total_salay = gross CTC (base+allowances before attendance adjustment); total_salary = net earned salary for the period. Two similar column names computing different financial concepts creates developer confusion and likely causes copy-paste errors in reports.
